    Splitting off the copies of S₋ #

    Tools for Step 2 of the proof of Theorem 5.2. Inside D, every T splits as T₀ ⊕ S₋^(I) with T₀ ∈ C (2.3) (DSplit.bicone); S₋^(I) is a coproduct of copies of S₋ in D, and I →₀ P a coproduct of copies of a module P. Bicones with isomorphic summands have isomorphic points, a positive finite factor cancels from cardinals, and the dimension of I →₀ P is |I| dim P. Also: S₋ is indecomposable in D_fin.
